result.reason: All three items constitute the Gemara's systematic elimination of candidate cases for Ilfa's dilemma — exactly what heading 0 ('Half-Pure Hands Query') describes as 'walking through a series of candidate cases, systematically eliminating each one before arriving at the genuine sha'alah,' while the current placement under 'Eliminating Cases' (index 1) only partially matches and its prose already describes the content of all three items anyway, making index 0 the more appropriate home for the full dilemma introduction including the cases.

All three items form a continuous chain about residual moisture (mashkeh tofeach / tofeach lehatfiach) and whether it constitutes chibur for hand-washing, which is precisely what the 'Moisture Remaining Case' prose describes.

The passage introduces the mikvah context and Rabbi Yehuda's chibur ruling as a possible limitation on the principle — exactly what heading 0 ('Chibur & Mikvah') describes as 'perhaps the chibur principle is known only in the context of a mikvah,' whereas heading 1 ('Rabbi Yehuda Chibur') describes the mikvah source and Rabbi Yehuda's ruling as already established context, suggesting those items precede the current placement.
The passage describes exactly the hybrid case (half by immersion, half by pouring) that results in teiku, which is precisely what the 'Half Immersion Half Pour' section's prose discusses.

The passage describes Rav Pappa's ruling about nine kabin for a sick ba'al keri and his dilemma about half-immersion/half-pouring ending in teiku, which exactly matches the 'Rav Papa Extension' section's prose about chetzyo be-tvila ve-chetzyo be-netina ending in teiku.

Both items together present Rabbi Yochanan's ruling that when two people are co-messengers (the get exits from both their hands), the get is valid, and the Gemara's inference that two co-messengers need not make the combined declaration — which is precisely what candidate 10 ('Two Messengers') discusses.

Items 1-3 are precisely Abaye's challenge resolved via the kiyum shetarot confusion concern (matching heading 2's prose), and items 4-9 continue as the alternative version and its resolution within the same analytical thread, making heading 2 the best single home for the entire passage.

The passage is the Gemara's question 've-liflog nami Rabbi Yehuda b'reisha' and Ulla's initial answer, which is precisely what candidate 4's prose describes as the logical pressure that motivates Ulla's teaching.

The passage is Rav Oshaya's objection to Ulla presenting the Baraita that Rabbi Yehuda validates 'this case but not another,' which is precisely what the 'Ulla Interpretation' prose section describes and analyzes.

The passage explicitly addresses the 'salka daatach amina' reasoning — why one might have thought Rabbi Yehuda would be lenient even in the one-witness case — which directly matches the 'Salka Daatach' section's prose about that exact reasoning.

The passage introduces Rav Yehuda's statement that two who brought a get from overseas brings us to the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis, which fits best under 'Salka Daatach' as the starting point of explaining why one might have thought otherwise about Rabbi Yehuda's position, rather than under the 'Final Resolution' section which discusses conclusions already reached.
